answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity strength a function of age and honest history, not a one-time signup. Every newborn account starts at zero weight and earns influence only by being attested across many consecutive epochs; a flood of fresh personas is weightless, because none has survived long enough to matter. Weight compounds slowly, like limestone building a karst, so standing cannot be bought at once. A truthful account becomes a sturdy walnut with an earned shell of reputation, while the idea that trust can be cloned is just a fable the ledger refutes.
